Denmark and Norway are small countries with millions of people where everyone knows each other. If you go to Denmark, you might know the prime minister or a friend who knows her. Small size builds cohesion. 

Number two: Denmark and Norway are cold places where people spend much time indoors together, becoming friends. Because it's so cold, they have to work together.

Third factor: These countries are surrounded by dangerous enemies like Germany, Russia, and Sweden. This teaches them the importance of sticking together and working as a team.

In Holland, you might think it’s very egalitarian, but it’s actually one of the most unequal places on Earth because aristocrats have a lot of money. However, they understand that if people are happy, they’re safer. So aristocrats promote welfare states to maintain social cohesion.

Athenians and Spartans didn't want to destroy each other but that led to Macedonia's rise. They didn't care because they thought they were invincible, which is due to hubris. An empire that recognizes it can fall will never fall.
